solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sounds like a reasonable concern

indicators.note: Sounds like tells the solver to say the phrase out loud and write down a word that is spoken the same way

parts.note: reasonable means fair, so the phrase is heard as A FAIR

explanation.surface: Someone voices what seems a perfectly sensible worry.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or business, something that is one's concern, as in 'that's my affair'.

clue.text: Guarantor detailed changes for crew member

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the remaining letters are rearranged
detailed here is de-tailed, with its tail or last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A financial backer amends the terms in fine detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'thorough', but means losing the tail: GUARANTO, which 'changes' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts were the crew of Jason's ship, the Argo, in Greek myth.

clue.text: Surprise fat brute crossing river with German

parts.note: flab is excess body fat

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the beast lies over the next pieces

parts.note: a brute is a beast

explanation.surface: A hefty thug wading a river with a German companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To flabbergast is to astonish someone completely.

clue.text: Heart-throb is not working on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: idle means not working

explanation.surface: A pin-up star is out of work but still on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a hugely admired celebrity, the kind fans swoon over.

clue.text: Gripping tale involved Hitler capturing leader of Lithuanian resistance

indicators.note: capturing says the jumbled name takes in the next piece and holds it inside
involved means tangled up or convoluted, so the dictator's name is jumbled
leader of points to the first letter of the word Lithuanian

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A wartime yarn about Hitler seizing the head of the Lithuanian partisans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' jumbles HITLER into THRILE, which 'capturing' wraps round L to make THRILLE; R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a story full of suspense, the kind of tale that grips the reader.

clue.text: Henry, playing catch up with journalist, moved quickly

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
playing a role means appearing as it, so playing gives as

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the word for catch is reversed

parts.note: to net is to catch
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A man called Henry, playing catch-up beside a reporter, hurried along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing catch up' reads as one idiom, but splits: 'playing' gives AS, as an actor plays a part.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to hurry, so hastened means went quickly.

clue.text: At home in Alabama undergoing examination of bowels

indicators.note: undergoing in a down clue means going under, so the last pieces sit below the test

parts.note: in means at home
a test is an examination
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A patient at home in Alabama has a bowel examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoing examination' reads as a medical check, but 'undergoing' places IN AL beneath TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestinal means relating to the intestines, which are the bowels.

clue.text: Liberal unveiled neon sign

indicators.note: unveiled means with its covering removed, so neon loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A political party reveals a new illuminated advertising sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neon sign' reads as a shop light; 'sign' is a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: US lawman called about uprising

parts.note: to call someone is to ring them, so called gives rang

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means rising up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An American sheriff telephoned to report a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reads as a revolt, but it reverses RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger, such as a Texas Ranger, is a law-enforcement officer in the United States.

clue.text: Fill empty container with uncooked meat

indicators.note: Fill means put something inside, so the emptied container takes in the next piece
empty means with the contents removed, so the container loses its middle

parts.note: a bin is a container
raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: An instruction to stock an empty tub with raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN also fits 'container', giving PRAWN, but a prawn is seafood rather than meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is meat from a pig's head set in jelly, and also means muscle.

clue.text: Essentially easygoing, moral training holds universal allure

indicators.note: Essentially means at its essence or core, so take the central letter of easygoing
holds says the rearranged letters keep the next piece within them
training means shaping or drilling, so the letters of moral are put into a new order

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A relaxed yet principled upbringing gives a person universal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' rearranges MORAL into LAMOR, which 'holds' U to make LAMOUR, after G from the heart of 'easygoing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is attractive charm or fascination, which is what allure means.

clue.text: Strike is about Democrat breaching settlement

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is is read backwards
breaching means breaking into, so one piece pierces the other

parts.note: a town is a settlement
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A political report of a walkout over a Democrat breaking an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like a deal ending the strike, but it is a place: TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-down is a protest in which workers occupy their workplace and refuse to work.

clue.text: Apprehends seaman between Norway and Sweden

indicators.note: between places the sailor in the gap separating the two country codes

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor is arrested on the border between two Scandinavian countries.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is informal for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Pole stifles sob before second race

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so the pole closes round the next pieces

parts.note: a stake is a wooden pole

indicators.note: before puts the weeping ahead of the second

parts.note: to sob is to weep

explanation.surface: A Polish competitor holds back tears before running a second race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with its capital looks like a person from Poland; it is a stake. A sweepstake is also a race where the winner takes all the stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake can be a horse race in which the owners' stakes go to the winners.

clue.text: Servicemen almost free comrades in revolt

indicators.note: in revolt means overturned or in upheaval, so the combined letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the word free loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers have nearly freed their mutinous comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts FREE to FRE; 'in revolt' rearranges FRE with COMRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are a nation's military services, made up of servicemen and women.

clue.text: Lumbered drunkenly round ancient city making terrible din

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go about the city
drunkenly means staggering about, so the letters of lumbered are jumbled

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A drunk staggered noisily around an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' rearranges LUMBERED into BLUEMDER, which goes 'round' UR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scream blue murder is to make a loud, furious outcry, so the phrase means a dreadful racket.

clue.text: Ill-disciplined peacekeepers mainly skulk around Yemen's capital

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are troops of the United Nations

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the shortened word is read backwards
mainly means for the most part, so the word for skulk loses its final letter

parts.note: to skulk is to lurk

indicators.note: capital means the head letter of the word Yemen's

explanation.surface: Undisciplined UN troops hang about near the Yemeni capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims LURK to LUR and 'around' turns it to RUL; 'capital' looks like Sana'a but gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly behaviour is disorderly and hard to control, the opposite of disciplined.

clue.text: Spiritualists introducing English detective to relatives

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another means bringing it inside, so the family members take in the pieces

parts.note: mums are relatives
DI is a detective inspector in the British police

explanation.surface: An English police detective is presented to a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediums are people who claim to pass messages from the dead, as practised in spiritualism.

clue.text: Parting from food and drink supplier

parts.note: fare is food, as in 'simple fare'
a well supplies water to drink

explanation.surface: Someone takes leave of a caterer who provides food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a leave-taking, an act of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Fresh fish consumed in hotel bar

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed up within, so the fish goes inside the hotel

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
sole is a flatfish
a T is a kind of bar, as in a T-bar

explanation.surface: Freshly caught fish is eaten in a hotel's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' reads as just-caught, but means cheeky. 'bar' gives T, from a T-bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean impudent or cheeky, so insolent is an apt synonym.

clue.text: It helps identify Spooner's domesticated horse

indicators.note: Spooner's refers to the Reverend Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: domesticated means tame
a nag is a horse, usually an old one

explanation.surface: A tame horse would help someone recognise it.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a label worn or attached to show who someone is.

clue.text: Retired doctor worried parent partaking in happy event

indicators.note: partaking in means taking part inside something, so the pieces sit within the word for happy

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy or carefree

indicators.note: Retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the abbreviation for doctor is read backwards
worried means troubled or fretted, so the letters of parent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retired GP fusses as a parent takes part in a joyful occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy event' reads as a birth, but 'happy' is GAY. 'Retired' turns DR to RD and 'worried' rearranges PARENT into ENPART.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden party is a social gathering held on a lawn, such as those at Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Rock band in advert provided entertainment

indicators.note: in places the band inside the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is an advert
Muse is an English rock band

explanation.surface: A rock group appears in a commercial and keeps viewers entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to entertain, so amused means gave entertainment.

clue.text: See 21
Cops keep schtum about article on extremely evil old man

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for silence goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to keep schtum is to stay quiet, to hush

indicators.note: on puts the article after the letters before it
extremely points to the outermost letters of the word evil

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Police stay silent about a newspaper piece on a very wicked elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives EL from 'evil' and 'on' sets A after it. Schtum comes from German stumm, silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years, so the name stands for any very old man.

clue.text: Network provides shelter for old vagabond

indicators.note: provides shelter for means takes in and covers, so the network holds the next piece

parts.note: HBO (Home Box Office) is a US television network

explanation.surface: A broadcaster gives refuge to an elderly homeless man.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a wandering homeless person, a tramp or vagrant.

clue.text: Graduate smuggling Ecstasy with university sweetheart

indicators.note: smuggling means hiding something inside, so the degree holder conceals the drug

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A graduate sneaks drugs into a college with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: Tack securing wide bandage

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the riding gear holds the next letter inside

parts.note: tack is a horse's gear, including the saddle
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A tack is used to fasten a broad strip of dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' looks like a small nail; it is horse equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle is to wrap tightly in cloth, as one binds a wound or a baby.

clue.text: Morning disrupted by setter? That's the intention!

indicators.note: disrupted by means broken into, so the morning has the setter put inside it

parts.note: AM stands for morning, ante meridiem
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The compiler cheerfully admits to deliberately ruining someone's morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a purpose or goal, which is what an intention is.

clue.text: Sticky substance rascal regularly concealed in palm, say

indicators.note: concealed in means hidden within, so the picked letters go inside the tree

parts.note: a palm is an example of a tree, as 'say' signals

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter of rascal

explanation.surface: A rogue hides a gooey substance in his hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palm' looks like the hand; 'say' shows it is an example of a tree. 'regularly' takes ACL from 'rascal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the thick, syrupy by-product of sugar refining, notably sticky.

clue.text: Protest in front of cathedral in prim manner

indicators.note: in front of puts the objection ahead of the cathedral

parts.note: to demur is to raise an objection or protest
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A demonstration outside a cathedral is conducted with great propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Demurely means modestly and reservedly, behaving in a prim, decorous way.

clue.text: Colour reflected in stalagmite's surface

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the end of one and the start of the next

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A colour shows up mirrored in the outer layer of a cave formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a reddish-brown shade, also the name of an apple of that hue.
